Key model recommendations (shortlist):
- redwood-ggml-13b-q4_0 (quantized) — best cost/quality balance for conversational summarization workloads.
  * Observed TPS (seq len 16): ~780 TPS on H100 (batching 4, async batching)
  * Latency: p50 24ms, p95 62ms, p99 120ms (end-to-end token generation on H100; includes KV-cache warmup)
- redwood-rlhf-30b-fp16 — higher quality; recommended for clinical note synthesis where hallucination risk must be minimized.
  * Observed TPS (seq len 24): ~210 TPS on A100-80GB
  * Latency: p50 48ms, p95 130ms, p99 260ms
- redwood-13b-edge-opt (low-CPU) — for Dedicated pools with constrained GPU density.

Quality/regression concerns we flagged during the evals:
- Truncation in long-context summaries: for prompts > 1,200 tokens we saw response cutoffs with the quantized 13b variant. Guard: increase max_new_tokens or use the 30b fallback for long syntheses.
- Entity hallucinations in discharge summaries: precision drops ~6% on the base 13b across the Chronicle test set when prompts use shorthand. Guard: prompt normalization step in the harness + a named-entity verification pass.
- Tokenization mismatch between your legacy ingestion pipeline and our runtime: we included a small grammar/whitespace normalizer in the prompt pack.

Great questions — answered inline below:

1) TPS measurement context: the 780 TPS figure is model-token throughput for seq len 16 measured on H100 in our benchmark harness (batching 4, async). For end-to-end generation of a 40-token response you should expect lower effective throughput (~160-220 requests/sec) because generation requires multiple autoregressive steps. For capacity planning we usually map to tokens/sec: 780 model-tokens/sec * (avg response 40 tokens) = ~19.5 requests/sec per replica under identical profiling assumptions. To hit sustained 200 requests/sec (40-token median) you would need ~10 replicas under the same hardware/config.

2) Regression harness cost: running your 1,000-sample smoke run across the three recommended models (13b quant, 13b-edge-opt, 30b fp16) using our hosted test credits would consume roughly: 13b-quant ~ $120, 13b-edge ~ $200, 30b-fp16 ~ $900 — total ~ $1,220. If you run on Dedicated capacity the unit costs change; we can provide a Dedicated quote once you pick target replicas.

3) p99 < 300ms for 40-token responses: with the current kernel selection and H100 profile, the redwood-13b-q4_0 hits p99 ~120ms in token generation for short sequences but end-to-end p99 for 40-token responses is around 450–520ms (depending on batching). The only model in our shortlist likely to meet p99 < 300ms end-to-end at 40 tokens is the 30b-fp16 when running on optimized H100 nodes with an aggressive batching/latency SLO config (and a 2-replica hot-warm cache to avoid cold KV-cache effects). If p99 < 300ms is a hard SLA, recommend we:
  - Use 30b-fp16 on H100 and enable KV-cache prewarm + prefer small fixed batches (1–2) for that route.
  - Keep a quantized 13b as fallback for cheaper tail traffic.

I'll get Sean to spin the sandbox keys and a small test cluster today. Vivek — can you confirm whether you'd like us to pre-queue the 30b runs overnight (incurs additional cost but gives a quick proof)?

Daniel — happy to set a 30-minute call tomorrow if procurement wants the cost breakout live.

Thanks,
Marissa
